newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-French stocks dive on Socialist poll rumours.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-French stocks dive on Socialist poll rumours.

text.p: French stocks plunged more than four percent at one point on Wednesday as rumours swept the market that privately commissioned polls showed the opposition Socialists were well placed for Sunday's runoff parliamentary elections.
While some other European markets bubbled to fresh trading highs during the morning, France went sharply downhill after starting slightly firmer.
The currency market saw the yen rise against the dollar, buoyed by rising Japanese bond yields and a 2.32 percent surge in Tokyo share prices.
Platinum and palladium prices also soared to fresh highs on news of an illegal strike at Anglo American Platinum Corp's Rustenburg mine in South Africa.
"The market has gone crazy. The market is very, very tight," said one dealer as palladium was fixed in London at a record $188.00, up from $177.50 on Tuesday afternoon.
But the French stock market provided the main drama, with the CAC-40 index falling by the largest amount in percentage terms in more than four years before struggling off its lows.
One French trader said the market was being bombarded by rumours and, with more private polls due on Thursday on the likely outcome of the National Assembly elections, the bourse was feeling fragile.
"We're hearing everything. You can't imagine," he said.
Brokers said the talk was that privately commissioned polls -- which may not be divulged publicly under French law -- showed the left in strong position.
They added that President Jacques Chirac's efforts to boost the ruling centre-right RPR-UDF coalition following its poor showing in the first round of voting last Sunday did not seem convincing.
Several European stock markets followed Wall Street into record territory during the morning before the French poll rumours hit bond markets, which in turn weighed on equities.

Fresh trading highs were recorded in Germany, Hong Kong, Australia, Austria, Spain and Amsterdam after Wall Street's record close on Tuesday night when a surge in technology stocks sent the Dow Industrial Average up 0.51 percent at 7,383.41.
Germany's 30-share DAX index pushed to a new trading high of 3,632.33 in early trade but went into retreat after failing to penetrate the psychologically important 3,700-point level.
By 1130 GMT the 30-share DAX index was down 34.22 points at 3,640.14.
Among individual stocks, insurance giant Allianz hung on to a rise of 2.8 marks to 373 but was well off highs reached after a positive 1997 outlook.
London investors were also cheered initially by Wall Street's strong performance, but went into a decline as events in France hit European bonds.
Fears that a French coalition of Socialist and Communists could scrap an austerity drive to qualify for Europe's monetary union if they won this weekend's vote, capped Bund and gilt gains.
The blue chip FTSE 100 index was down 7.1 points at 4,674.5 by mid-session.

Jittery bond markets on both sides of the Atlantic continued to weigh on investor enthusiasm, dealers said. U.S. treasuries slipped in New York on Tuesday,with the yield on the benchmark 30-year long bond closing above the seven percent level at 7.02 percent.

"The bonds are still a bit of a worry for this market," the head of trading at a large brokerage said. "The last time they crept above the seven percent mark we had a big sell-off on Wall Street. The bonds may be telling us that the Dow is near another peak and needs to cool down a bit."
On the currency front, analysts said that while higher Japanese bond yields and the jump in the Nikkei had helped to boost the yen against the dollar, its gains were seen as limited.
Against the mark, the dollar remained steady and above 1.70 marks on concerns over a broad-based start to European economic and monetary union (EMU), they said.
"The dollar is being supported by increasing fears of a soft EMU," said Brian Martin, chief forex economist at BZW in London.
CURRENCIES AT 1130 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.7026 marks and 115.91 yen compared with 1.7045 marks and 116.50 yen in late European trading on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1130 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was down 7.1 points, or 0.15 percent, at 4,674.5.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 91.58, or 3.42 percent, at 2,588.76.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 34.22 points, or 0.93 percent, at 3,640.14.
PRECIOUS METALS
Palladium fixed at a record $188.00, compared with $177.50 on Tuesday afternoon after news a strike in South Africa.
Platinum fixed at $404.50, highest since August 1996, while gold was slightly firmer at $345.10, up $1.35. Silver was two cents stronger at $4.77.
